polityNote: Côte d'Ivoire, first-level units drawn as unions of the 510 sub-prefectures of geoBoundaries CIV ADM3 (CNTIG/OCHA 2021, CC BY 3.0 IGO). Each sub-prefecture is placed by the department it lies in (Wikipedia list, oldid 1354427979) and that department's split history (statoids; department articles); statoids notes that department splits keep sub-prefectures whole. Layers: 49 departments (from decree 86-1021, 1986-09-24) → ten regions (decree 91-10, 1991-12-16) → sixteen regions (decree 97-18, 1997-01-15) → nineteen (2000) → twelve districts + two autonomous districts (decree 2011-263, 2011-09-28) → 31 regions + two autonomous districts (law 2014-451, 2014-08-05). Independent checks (①): the 19 regions of 2000 against the statoids areas give ratios 0.975–1.017 (total 322,974 vs 322,921 km², 1.000); 504 of 510 sub-prefectures fall in the same 2000 region of Natural Earth admin-1 by point sampling (the others: the three sub-prefectures of Grand-Bassam department, which NE places in Lagunes; two coastal slivers outside NE; Aboisso-Comoé at 0.6); the 49 departments against statoids' rounded 1995 areas give a median ratio of 1.00 (0.89–1.08, Aboisso 1.14); sub-prefecture → 2016 region (geoBoundaries ADM2) and → 2016 district (ADM1) agree for all 510. 'Parc National de Bona' is the part of Comoé National Park in Bounkani that has no sub-prefecture; it is carried with Bouna department (from which Doropo and Téhini were split around it in 2011).
